categories.name: Mortgage brokers (spousal buyouts & refinancing)
categories.opportunity: When one spouse wants to keep the home, they must refinance to buy the other out, and lenders generally require a signed separation agreement before funding. Brokers meet separating clients early and need the legal side done properly and promptly.
categories.rationale: The broker's file cannot close until the separation agreement exists, so they actively need a responsive family lawyer. Clients also come to lawyers needing financing advice, so referrals run both ways.

triggers.event: A separating client asks a broker whether they can keep the home
triggers.whyNeed: A separation agreement must be negotiated and signed before refinancing

triggers.event: Your client needs to know whether they can afford to keep the home
triggers.whyNeed: A financing pre-assessment informs the negotiation
triggers.partnerValue: A qualified financing client for the broker

categories.mutualValue: Brokers close refinances; you receive clients who need agreements. Your clients make better-informed settlement decisions.
categories.approach: Meet two or three brokers who handle spousal buyouts and agree on what each needs from the other and on timelines. Co-author a one-page 'keeping the home after separation' explainer.
categories.regulatoryNote: Mortgage brokers are regulated too. Referral relationships for lawyers and paralegals are regulated by the law society. Paying or receiving anything of value from non-licensees for referrals is generally prohibited, and licensee-to-licensee referral fees carry conditions such as client disclosure and limits. Build these relationships on expertise and reciprocity, and verify against current rules.

assumptions: People rarely start with a family lawyer. They start with a counsellor, a mortgage broker, an accountant, an EAP, or a friend. The professionals who see the separation first shape who gets called.
Family law has strong reciprocal intersections with criminal, immigration, estate, and tax matters. Lawyers in those areas meet family-law clients at urgent moments.
No typical project value was provided, so commercial-value ratings are relative to the industry, not your own pricing.

guardrails.title: Referral compensation
guardrails.body: Referral relationships for lawyers and paralegals are regulated by the law society. Paying or receiving anything of value from non-licensees for referrals is generally prohibited, and licensee-to-licensee referral fees carry conditions such as client disclosure and limits. Build these relationships on expertise and reciprocity, and verify against current rules.

guardrails.title: Partnerships are not paid-referral arrangements
guardrails.body: This analysis recommends building relationships based on mutual value. It does not assume that referral fees, commissions, exclusivity, or endorsements are permitted in your industry. Check professional, regulatory, and contractual rules before compensating anyone for referrals.

guardrails.title: Outreach in Canada: CASL applies
guardrails.body: Commercial electronic messages generally need express or implied consent, sender identification, and a working unsubscribe mechanism. Implied consent can exist when a business email address is conspicuously published, the message relates to the recipient's role, and they have not said they don't want such messages. Keep records of how consent was obtained. Personal information you collect is also subject to privacy law (e.g. PIPEDA).

guardrails.title: No automated outreach
guardrails.body: This tool does not contact anyone on your behalf. Every introduction should be personal, relevant to the recipient, and easy to decline.
